svg.title: What PlanRetrieveJob reads, changes and returns
svg.desc: Read-only inputs, the context it changes in place, local scratch state, the return value, and the external side effects some job methods have.
svg.metadata: ["The declaration: a context pointer, the job's payload id and its job_index go in; a {success, message, retain_job} tuple comes out. That is all the signature tells you.", "Read-only inputs flow in: Scheduler members (layout_, gg_), the job's fields and ctx->initial_state. ctx->disabledness_filters is meant to be read, but operator[] can insert a key.", "Inside, the method builds a local working_state: a copy of initial_state with the existing events applied. Its edits (e.g. setting the bay to READY_TO_RETRIEVE) touch only this copy.", "The shared ScheduleContext is read and written through ctx while the method runs: before this first job, ctx->events and last_entity_event are empty.", "After the call: four new events (all job_index 0), five edges and three last_entity_event entries. This is the real output, and none of it appears in the return type.", "The return value only reports the outcome: {true, \"\", false} on success, or {false, msg, retain_job} so Dispatch can keep a job that cannot run yet.", "Some job methods also reach outside the plan: PlanInsertJob sends a bay-reset request to Dispatch during expansion, and Plan() fires clean_garage_request_fn_ on an INSERT failure.", "A sketch of a pure alternative (not in the code): return the events, edges and follow-up requests as a value and let Plan() commit them, so the signature shows everything."]
